Q: Is there a quick way to edit snippets for the current language? A:

The most relevant looking command I can see is workbench.action.openSnippets, which is just the command that opens the quick pick to select which snippet scope file to open. I'm going to guess from looking at its signature at the time of this writing (which doesn't appear to take any arguments to specify a language identifier) that the answer is no, but I'd be happy to be wrong. Even if it did, if I recall correctly, keyboard shortcut args don't support variable expansion. And I'm not aware of a way to make keyboard shortcuts manipulate the contents of the input field of a quick pick (semi-related: Is there a keyboard shortcut command for typing specified text into input boxes (not the editor) in VS Code?).

Perhaps if you wanted this, you could raise a feature request asking for a new command to be added that does this.

Q: Missing first month in bar chart using R and Rstudio A:

The issue happens because your Month column is likely being read as a character string (text) rather than a proper Date object. When you pass a string directly into month(Month), lubridate fails to parse it correctly, causing the months to shift forward by one (turning January into February, and February into March).

Q: How to process each page of a multi-page PDF in place with imagemagick? A:

This should do what you want in ImageMagick 6 in one command line. You have to use -layers composite and separate your pdf and your blur processing by null:. This is the same process as merging animated gifs.

convert -density 288 image.pdf -write mpr:img null: \( mpr:img -blur 0x64 \) -compose minus -layers composite -channel RGB -negate -resize 25% image_deblurred.pdf

For Imagemagick 7, change convert to magick.

Q: How can I make developers override one of the two methods of an interface? A:

Possible options for the implementer to override methods to prevent recurse call and stack overflow...

1- Define seperate Interfaces for Kotlin or Java so implementers choose the appropriate API.

2- Throw by default instead of delegating

interface MyInterface {

fun process(callback: Consumer<MyClass>) {

throw UnsupportedOperationException(

"Override this function"

)

}

@JvmSynthetic

fun process(callback: (MyClass) -> Unit) {

throw UnsupportedOperationException(

"Override this function"

)

}

}

This approach fails fast instead of causing a stack overflow

The ideal design is to have one abstract method and one adapter method.

Q: Optimizing Fixed-Point Sqrt A:

Reinventing the wheel, really, and not in a good way. The correct solution is to calculate 1/sqrt(x) using Newton–Raphson (NR), and then multiply once to get x/sqrt(x) - just check for x==0 up front.

The reason why this is so much better is that the NR step for y=1/sqrt(x) is just y = (3-x*y*y)*y/2. That's all straightforward multiplication.
